meta.title: Pyright raises type error when supplying an attr field with both default and a validator
meta.fix_ref: none named (maintainer: 'This is addressed in pyright 1.1.374'; the parenthesis dependence was fixed in the release after 1.1.367)
meta.build_notes: npm pyright@1.1.367 (2024-06-12, the reporter's version) and pyright@1.1.374 (2024-07-31), the release the maintainer names for the fix.
meta.notes: Mechanism differs from the screening class (R5 whitespace): the false positive is reported on a fresh open of the issue's first code block, without any transformation; the parentheses variant (the R5 aspect, which the maintainer calls a separate bug fixed one release after 1.1.367) is not probed. Uses the attrs package installed for the session interpreter (attrs 25.4.0, user site-packages); the reporter's attrs version is not stated.

settings_note: The issue names no settings (pyright CLI defaults); the session defaults apply; attrs is resolved from the session interpreter (python3 on PATH).

files.source: issue body, first python code block

repro.steps: Open main.py (an attrs class whose field has both a default and a validator). Reported: pyright reports an error for 'attrs.field(default=False, validator=attrs.validators.instance_of(bool))' although the code is correct (mypy reports nothing; the maintainer confirms the bug). Probe: no error-severity diagnostic may be reported for main.py.
